text:
Edmonton's first season under Mike Babcock has a strange shape. The Oilers are 17-5-4 with 38 points and a 97% playoff chance in our race model, yet they have just 49.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against). They have scored 25.88 more goals than those chances predict, and our numbers put them 9.8 points ahead of what their play has earned. Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl explain most of that gap: with Vasily Podkolzin they have outscored teams 22-8, and Draisaitl is in the Rocket Richard race.

The last week was the reminder. A road trip ended with a shootout loss in St. Louis on Sunday, three games without a win (0-2-1), and the chances back that up: 42% of the expected goals. The depth is the problem. The Mathieu Joseph, Alex Formenton and Owen Michaels trio has 31% of the expected goals and has been outscored 11-5.

In net, the news is better. Devon Levi, acquired from Buffalo in July, won 10 of his first 11 games, and Tristan Jarry has saved 6.2 goals above expected over his last five starts. Jake Walman, back in the lineup Sunday, keeps showing up in trade talk.

What to watch: whether the Oilers find a second wave that holds its own, because a team this reliant on one line can't count on outscoring its chances by this much all year.
headline: The Oilers' record runs well ahead of their play
